quiz_item.question: When reverse-engineering a household appliance or mechanical device for Engineering Requirement 1, why do engineers apply the iterative engineering design process rather than building a single final product without testing?
options: A. Because engineers are prohibited from calculating loads, materials, or costs until after the product is sold to the public.

B. Because defining requirements, modeling subsystems (mechanical, electrical, structural), building prototypes, testing failure modes, and iterating on data reveals trade-offs in safety, efficiency, and manufacturability before mass production.
C. Because reverse engineering means copying only the exterior paint color of a product while ignoring how its internal gears and circuits operate.
D. Because the engineering design process eliminates the need for mathematics, physics, or safety standards.
choices: A. Because engineers are prohibited from calculating loads, materials, or costs until after the product is sold to the public.

B. Because defining requirements, modeling subsystems (mechanical, electrical, structural), building prototypes, testing failure modes, and iterating on data reveals trade-offs in safety, efficiency, and manufacturability before mass production.
C. Because reverse engineering means copying only the exterior paint color of a product while ignoring how its internal gears and circuits operate.
D. Because the engineering design process eliminates the need for mathematics, physics, or safety standards.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Because defining requirements, modeling subsystems (mechanical, electrical, structural), building prototypes, testing failure modes, and iterating on data reveals trade-offs in safety, efficiency, and manufacturability before mass production.

Design Engineer Problem Solving: The design engineer uses new and existing ideas to solve a new problem or to solve an old problem in a new way (p. 38).
Meeting Project and Budget Goals: These engineers find solutions that work according to the project's requirements, stay within the budget, and are easy and safe to use (p. 38).
Sustainable and Repairable Solutions: The solutions must be doable, long-lasting, practical to maintain or repair, and environmentally safe (p. 38).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Discuss Project Budget Constraints: These engineers find solutions that work according to the project's requirements, stay within the budget, and are easy and safe to use (p. 38).
Step 2 - Review Maintenance and Safety: The solutions must be doable, long-lasting, practical to maintain or repair, and environmentally safe (p. 38).
Step 3 - Examine Mathematical Modeling Roles: The analytical engineer is mainly responsible for creating mathematical models of physical problems (p. 38).
Step 4 - Explore Physical Behavior Simulations: Analysis is the process of using the methods and tools of mathematics to simulate (mimic) how a physical object will behave in response (p. 38).

requirements.req_text: Do TWO of the following: (a) Transforming Motion. Using common materials or a construction set, make a simple model that will demonstrate motion. Explain how the model uses basic mechanical elements like levers and inclined planes to demonstrate motion. Describe an example where this mechanism is used in a real product. (b) Using Electricity. Make a list of 10 electrical appliances in your home. Find out approximately how much electricity each uses in one month. Learn how to find out the amount and cost of electricity used in your home during periods of light and heavy use. List five ways to conserve electricity. (c) Understanding Electronics. Using an electronic device such as a smartphone or tablet computer, find out how sound, video, text or images travel from one location to another. Explain how the device was designed for ease of use, function, and durability. (d) Using Materials. Do experiments to show the differences in strength and heat conductivity in wood, metal, and plastic. Discuss with your counselor what you have learned. (e) Converting Energy. Do an experiment to show how mechanical, heat, chemical, solar, and/or electrical energy may be converted from one or more types of energy to another. Explain your results. Describe to your counselor what energy is and how energy is converted and used in your surroundings. (f) Moving People. Find out the different ways people in your community get to work. Make a study of traffic flow (number of vehicles and relative speed) in both heavy and light traffic periods. Discuss with your counselor what might be improved to make it easier for people in your community to get where they need to go. (g) Building an Engineering Project. Enter a project in a science or engineering fair or similar competition. (This requirement may be met by participation on an engineering competition project team.) Discuss with your counselor what your project demonstrates, the kinds of questions visitors to the fair asked you, and how well you were able to answer their questions.

Technical and Ethical Standards: Engineers are also professionals because they make their living in an activity that conforms to the technical and ethical standards of a profession (p. 91).
Ethics in Evolving Technology: Ethics are an important part of the engineering profession, especially as science and technology continue to evolve rapidly (p. 91).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: When reverse-engineering a household appliance or mechanical device for Engineering Requirement 1, why do engineers apply the iterative engineering design process rather than building a single final product without testing?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: When reverse-engineering a household appliance or mechanical device for Engineering Requirement 1, why do engineers apply the iterative engineering design process rather than building a single final product without testing?
options: A. Because engineers are prohibited from calculating loads, materials, or costs until after the product is sold to the public.

B. Because defining requirements, modeling subsystems (mechanical, electrical, structural), building prototypes, testing failure modes, and iterating on data reveals trade-offs in safety, efficiency, and manufacturability before mass production.
C. Because reverse engineering means copying only the exterior paint color of a product while ignoring how its internal gears and circuits operate.
D. Because the engineering design process eliminates the need for mathematics, physics, or safety standards.
choices: A. Because engineers are prohibited from calculating loads, materials, or costs until after the product is sold to the public.

B. Because defining requirements, modeling subsystems (mechanical, electrical, structural), building prototypes, testing failure modes, and iterating on data reveals trade-offs in safety, efficiency, and manufacturability before mass production.
C. Because reverse engineering means copying only the exterior paint color of a product while ignoring how its internal gears and circuits operate.
D. Because the engineering design process eliminates the need for mathematics, physics, or safety standards.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Because defining requirements, modeling subsystems (mechanical, electrical, structural), building prototypes, testing failure modes, and iterating on data reveals trade-offs in safety, efficiency, and manufacturability before mass production.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Engineers analyze how mechanical, electrical, and control subsystems interact and use iterative prototyping and testing to optimize performance, reliability, cost, and safety constraints.
